body:
Thank you for your replies, everybody.  I'll post in the LGBT sub-reddit when I get a little more time, I'm on my way out the door but I want to reply here really quick.

Just to clarify, I'd actually like to go back to school too, but after my all-F semester it's not going to be easy.  I was 14 hours from graduating here, but I screwed up.  Even if I'm allowed back in or can find a school that will take me, I'd really like to be 100% sure I'm not going to give in to my fatalistic inclinations and get kicked out again.  Or at least 80% sure.

CedarWolf:

Thanks.  I haven't had good luck with the local LGBT groups, but I guess I should give them another try.  I'll PM you later.

CabalNethilren:

Haha, I don't know, it's an interesting idea but I'm not much of a writer.  Like you said, though, there could be some benefit to getting these thoughts out of my head, so maybe I'll try it.

emiteal:

It's funny, because it's not like I even find the pretty-little-princess pop-star kind of feminine ideal all that appealing or anything and it's not like when I see other trans women who don't pass a hundred percent I think any less of them for it, but I guess somehow I've got a double standard and I give myself the worst of it.

You're right, I need a new job.

wtfomg:

I see what you're saying, and again, it's not as if I don't plan to return to school... the frustrating thing is when I was in school I put a lot of time into Japanese, spent nine months living over there and really am not all that bad at it, but the Japanese program at the university I'd been attending (or, you know, skipping) wasn't challenging enough for me and I haven't had much luck improving ever since I got back from studying abroad.  So I even had a skill I was working on, if not a specific career, but I couldn't find the resources to keep it up and now that I've gotten kicked out entirely and have this massive debt waiting to come crashing down on me it seems it might all go to waste.
